key_insight: BugGen 2.0 makes RTL bug synthesis more efficient by assigning structural decisions and validation to deterministic algorithms while reserving LLMs for localized semantic rewriting.
engineering_relevance: Lower inference and simulation costs can help scale ground-truth RTL bug datasets for debugging tools and testbench evaluation.
method: Use deterministic algorithms for structural analysis, mutation-target selection, and validation.
Use LLMs to generate localized semantic mutations.
Expand accepted bug locations with alternative mutations, simulating a subset to estimate acceptance for the rest.
evidence_signal: Across four OpenTitan IP blocks and FabScalar with three LLMs, BugGen 2.0 met every requested quota of compilable bugs causing at least two test failures; completed same-model comparisons showed 6.8×–15.4× lower token use than BugGen 1.0.
watch_item: Acceptance estimates do not verify individual unsimulated variants; full simulation accepted 77.7% of AES variants and 95.2% of FabScalar variants.
paper_title: BugGen 2.0: Rethinking the Roles of LLMs for Scalable RTL Bug Synthesis
